title: Kris Joseph

{{Infobox NCAA athlete | color = #FF6F00; border:2px solid #212B6D | fontcolor = white | name = Kris Joseph | image = KrisJoseph.JPG | college = [[Syracuse Orange basketball|Syracuse]] | sport = [[Basketball]] | position = [[Small forward]] | class = Senior | career_start = 2008 | jersey = 32 | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 7 | weight_lb = 218 | nationality = [[Canada]] | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1988|12|17|mf=yes}} | birth_place = [[Montreal, Quebec]] | highschool = Archbishop Carroll (D.C.) }} '''Kristopher Joseph''' (born December 17, 1988) is a [[Canada|Canadian]] basketball player who played for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball]] team from 2008 to 2012.http://www.nbadraft.net/players/kris-joseph Kris is the brother of ex-Michigan State and [[Vermont Catamounts men's basketball]] player, Maurice Joseph. Maurice is now the Assistant Director of Basketball Operations at George Washington University in Washington, DC. He is the son of parents, Eartha and Michael Joseph, both born in [[Trinidad and Tobago]]. Kris is also second cousin to brothers [[Cory Joseph]], a reserve guard for the San Antonio Spurs, and Devoe Joseph, who was the leading scorer for the [[Oregon Ducks]] of the [[Pacific-12 Conference]] during the 2011-2012 season. == Early life == Kris Joseph is a native of [[Montreal]], [[Quebec]], where he grew up in the working-class neighbourhood of [[Cote-des-Neiges]] north of downtown. Joseph first picked up a basketball in Grade 2 but was forced to shoot on garbage cans with his older brother Maurice due to a lack of courts in his low-income neighbourhood. A court was eventually erected in Cote-des-Neiges and the brothers battled for hours.http://www.qhoops.net/articles/article.jsp?aId=755 == High School == Kris played in Maurice's shadow for a number of years as the older star gained prominence at noted Montreal-area prep school Champlain St. Lambert College.http://www.qhoops.net/articles/article.jsp?aId=734 Kris struggled at first against elite competition, getting cut from his club team at the age of 14. He worked on his game, grew to 6-foot-6 and became a star for Sun Youth, a club-team powerhouse in the Montreal Basketball League.http://www.qhoops.net/articles/article.jsp?aId=755 As a tenth-grader, he led the Quebec provincial team to a silver medal at the 2005 Canada Games.http://montreal.ctv.ca/servlet/an/local/CTVNews/20100318/mtl_josephs_ncaa100318/20100318/?hub=MontrealSports On a recommendation from youth coach Henry Wong, who thought Joseph needed an athletic and academic challenge, Joseph's mother agreed to let him leave Montreal in 2006 to complete two years of high school at Archbishop Carroll in Washington, D.C.http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2012/03/kris_joseph_road_winds_from_mo.html As a senior, Joseph led Archbishop Carroll to a 26-11 record, including a 21 point, five rebound, three assist and three block effort in the Washington Catholic Athletic Conference (WCAC) Tournament in a 65-55 win over Our Lady of Good Counsel. Joseph was also invited to play in the Baltimore All-Stars vs. U.S. All-Stars Exhibition in April. That season, Joseph would go on to earn 2008 second team honors from the [[Washington Post]].http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=2692&sport=176&roster=228&path=mbasket He played [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball with the DC Assault. == College == Joseph was ranked 114th overall and the 17th small forward in the class of 2008 by Rivals.com while garnering offers from [[Georgetown Hoyas|Georgetown]] and [[University of Maryland, College Park]] before settling on Syracuse.http://www.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=60727&Sport=2http://media.www.dailyorange.com/media/storage/paper522/news/2008/04/01/Sports/Mbb-he.Can.Play.Everywhere.At.6Foot8.Kris.Joseph.Has.Plenty.Of.Versatility.With-3294099.shtml === 2008–09 === Joseph would see early playing time, including seven points in 22 minutes in an 85-51 rout of [[Le Moyne College|Le Moyne]] on November 16, 2008 http://www.auburnpub.com/articles/2008/11/17/sports/sports05.txt and a 13-point six rebound effort in a 86-66 victory against Oakland University on November 22, 2008.http://www.democratandchronicle.com/article/20081122/SPORTS09/811220326/1007/SPORTS On November 24, 2008, Joseph's 10 points and five rebounds helped then-unranked Syracuse upset then-No. 18 Florida, 89-83, in the semi-finals of the [[CBE Classic]].http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=283290183 After an injury to [[Paul Harris (basketball)|Paul Harris]], Joseph would receive the first start of his career against [[South Florida University|South Florida]] on January 2, 2009, scoring seven points and adding three rebounds.http://www.syracuse.com/axeman/index.ssf/2009/01/susouth_florida_recap_1.html === 2009–10 === Joseph would become a key reserve in his second year at Syracuse. In SU's Big East opener against [[Seton Hall University|Seton Hall]] on December 29, 2009, Joseph scored 16 points, including 8-of-9 shooting from the free throw line in a 80-73 win.http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=293642550 On January 6, 2010 against Memphis, Joseph scored 15 second half points to go along with nine rebounds in a 74-57 win.http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=300070183 Joseph finished with averages of 11.0 points and 5.4 rebounds on the season, and was named the Big East Conference Sixth Man of the Year.http://suathletics.syr.edu/news/2010/3/8/JosephBE3.8.10.aspx === 2010–11 === Joseph gained national prominence as a go-to scorer for the Orange during his junior year. He was named to the Wooden Award Preseason Top 50 list and improved his numbers across the board, leading Syracuse in scoring at 14.3 points per game and placing second in rebounding (5.2) and steals (1.5). He was named to the All-Big East third team, the first Canadian to receive the honour since fellow Montrealer [[Bill Wennington]] in 1985.http://www.redstormsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/100511aaa.html http://suathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7750&path=mbasket http://www.qhoops.net/articles/article.jsp?aId=1341 === 2011-12 === Joseph was once again named to the Wooden Award Preseason Top 50 list as a senior.http://suathletics.com/news/2011/11/7/MBB_1107113314.aspx?path=mbasket His final season started off with a flourish as he was named the Big East Player of the Week after leading his Syracuse Orange to the NIT Season Tip Off Championship. Joseph was named Most Outstanding Player of the tournament with averages of 19.0 points, 9.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals in wins against Virginia Tech and Stanford.http://suathletics.com/news/2011/11/25/MBB_1125110943.aspx?path=mbasket He led the Orange in scoring during the regular season (13.4 ppg) and received an array of post-season awards, including a spot on the 2012 All-Big East First Team. Joseph is the first Canadian-born player ever to be named to the first team of that conference.http://www.torontosun.com/2012/03/04/joseph-makes-history-with-big-east-nod He was named an AP Honorable Mention All-American http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/18064597/ap-allamerica-teams and also earned spots on the USBWA All District II team as well as the NABC All-District 5 First Team. Additionally, Joseph was one of 15 post-season finalists for the Wooden Award, making him among the most decorated Canadians ever to play NCAA Division I basketball. With his 15 points against Manhattan on Nov. 14, 2011, Joseph became the 55th player at Syracuse to score 1,000 points.http://www.suathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7750&path=mbasket He concluded his storied career with 10 points, two rebounds and 3 steals in Syracuse's 77-70 loss to Ohio State in the Elite Eight. Joseph is projected as a late first-round pick in the 2012 NBA Draft.http://nbadraft.net/early-mock-draft == References == {{Reflist|2}} == External links == * [http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=2692&sport=176&roster=228&path=mbasket SUAthletics.com]
